clue.text: Had meal in bar, fed steak specially cooked

indicators.note: something specially cooked has been prepared afresh, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone ate at a bar where a steak was given special treatment in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'specially cooked' rearranges all eleven letters of BAR FED STEAK.
explanation.definitionFit: To breakfast is to eat the morning meal, so the past tense means had a meal.

clue.text: Authentic Spanish football team

definitions.meaning: ... Madrid, or ... Sociedad, Spanish clubs whose names begin with the word for royal

explanation.surface: A claim that some Spanish side is the genuine article.
explanation.definitionFit: Real is a synonym of genuine, and Real Madrid is Spain's most famous football club.

clue.text: Birds, as seen around GB & NI

indicators.note: around tells us the word as is wrapped about the other piece

parts.note: taken as written
Great Britain and Northern Ireland together make the United Kingdom, UK

explanation.surface: Some seabirds spotted around the coasts of the British Isles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'GB & NI' is Great Britain plus Northern Ireland, which together form the United Kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Auks are a family of diving seabirds including puffins and guillemots.

clue.text: Early form of cover in garden?

definitions.text: Early form of cover in garden?

parts.words: Early form of cover in garden?
parts.note: in Genesis Adam and Eve sewed leaves of a tree together to cover themselves in Eden, the very first garment

explanation.surface: Sounds like a gardening question about mulch or ground cover.
explanation.walkthrough: The garden is Eden, and the cover is the first clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The leaf Adam and Eve used to hide their nakedness in Eden is the earliest garment in the Bible.

clue.text: Old bob had a meal, becoming replete

definitions.note: here the rare verb sense, to fill to the full, which is why it matches a verb

parts.note: bob was slang for a shilling, abbreviated s in pre-decimal British money
ate means had a meal

explanation.surface: Someone called Bob, getting on in years, ate until full.
explanation.walkthrough: A bob was a British shilling before 1971, written s.
explanation.definitionFit: To fill someone completely with food is to satisfy their appetite fully, a synonym pair.

clue.text: Attendant always accommodating queen on railway

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means sitting above the next piece
accommodating means holding within, so one piece takes in the other

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: A servant who always makes room for the monarch on the train.
explanation.walkthrough: EER (e'er, always) is 'accommodating' QU, with RY placed below in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An equerry is an officer of the royal household who attends a member of the royal family.

clue.text: Famous Greek's past, being involved in wild hen party

indicators.note: being involved in means one piece is set inside the other
wild suggests something out of control, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: ago means in the past

explanation.surface: A celebrated Greek has a history of joining raucous hen parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' scrambles HEN PARTY, and AGO ('past') is 'being involved in' it. A hen party is a British bachelorette party.
explanation.definitionFit: Pythagoras of Samos, the mathematician, was the founder of a school; a follower is so called.

clue.text: Architect of church overlooking river — enter and worship animatedly

indicators.note: in a down clue, overlooking puts the first piece above the next
doing something animatedly is doing it in a lively, agitated way, so the letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: A designer's church above a river invites people in to worship with gusto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'animatedly' rearranges ENTER and WORSHIP; 'and' just links them.
explanation.definitionFit: The man named was the English designer of St Paul's Cathedral in London.

clue.text: Not entirely gloomy, this old story?

indicators.note: not entirely tells us only part of the words is used, a run of letters sitting within them

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a rather sombre old tale is truly depressing.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional tale of gods or heroes is a legend from long ago.

clue.text: Holiday all wrapped up?

parts.note: a trip where flights, hotel and outings are all bundled together for one price, like a parcel

explanation.surface: Reads like a gift-wrapped present of a vacation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrapped up' suggests a parcel and also 'all arranged in advance'.
explanation.definitionFit: An inclusive holiday sold as a single bundle is a parcel in the second sense.

clue.text: Article, not English, by excellent Asian

indicators.note: not means the named letter is left out of the word

parts.note: the is the definite article
A1 means first-class, excellent, read as AI

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece, not about England, by a top-notch writer from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: THE loses E to give TH; A1 (first-rate) is written AI.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Thailand is an Asian person, a native of a southeast Asian country.

clue.text: Noticed boy — sweet, fatty type?

parts.note: spotted means noticed
Dick is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Someone caught sight of a plump lad with a sweet tooth.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'sweet, fatty type' is a pudding, not a person: suet is the fat.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a classic British steamed suet pudding studded with currants, served as dessert.

clue.text: Philosopher anti-ritual, I suspect

indicators.note: suspect, as an adjective, means dubious or not right, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone guesses a certain thinker opposed ritual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' rearranges ANTI-RITUAL plus I.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Bentham and Mill's ethics of the greatest happiness is called this.

clue.text: German city in which large amounts of money will go to mother

indicators.note: will go to says one piece is followed by the next

parts.note: pots of money means a great deal of it
dam is a mother, especially of animals

explanation.surface: A city where great fortunes are left to someone's mum.
explanation.definitionFit: Potsdam is the capital of Brandenburg, near Berlin, an example of a German city.

clue.text: Test after master's first lesson

indicators.note: after puts the test after the other piece
first means take just the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: an oral is a spoken exam, a test

explanation.surface: A spoken exam follows the teacher's opening class.
explanation.definitionFit: The moral of a story is the lesson it teaches.

clue.text: Awful row before criminal thug gets knocked into shape

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the next
awful suggests something messed up, so the letters of row are scrambled
criminal, used loosely as bad or wrong, signals that these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nasty quarrel ends with a lawless heavy being beaten up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' rearranges ROW as WRO and 'criminal' rearranges THUG as UGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrought metal has been worked or hammered into form, the old past tense of work.

clue.text: As vehicle, continue moving from side to side

parts.note: to wag is to move to and fro, like a dog's tail
on, as in carry on, means continue

explanation.surface: Someone told to keep swaying while in a cart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' is only a link: the clue reads 'as vehicle, (it is) wag on'.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagon is a four-wheeled cart, a kind of vehicle.

clue.text: Supporting flanks of army in attack

parts.note: to be for something is to support it

indicators.note: the flanks of a body are its sides, so take the outside letters

explanation.surface: Backing the wings of a force in an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: A foray is a sudden raid or sortie into enemy territory.

clue.text: Work without moving, head hidden

indicators.note: with its head hidden the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: still means without moving

explanation.surface: Someone toils motionless with their face out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: STILL loses its first letter S.
explanation.definitionFit: To till land is to work it by ploughing or digging.

clue.text: Endless rubbish produced by day out?

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: tripe is nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: Questioning whether a day out generated non-stop nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: TRIPE loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An outing or excursion lasting a day is a short journey.

clue.text: Word to describe key army officer

definitions.meaning: a musical key is either this or minor, as in C ___

explanation.surface: A term for an important soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a musical mode and a military rank between captain and lieutenant colonel.

clue.text: Rope in the sea, short length being submerged

indicators.note: being submerged means sinking into something, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: marine relates to the sea, and the marine is the sea world
L is the short form of length

explanation.surface: A line lost in the ocean, a bit of it sinking.
explanation.walkthrough: L ('short length') is 'being submerged' in MARINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Marline is thin two-strand cord used by sailors for binding, a type of line.

clue.text: Understanding about a type of noise

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a ding is a ringing sound

explanation.surface: Comprehending something about a particular sound.
explanation.definitionFit: One's reading of a situation is one's interpretation or grasp of it.

clue.text: Then surprisingly right, a learner brings delight

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests an unexpected arrangement of the letters

parts.note: L is for learner, as on British L-plates

explanation.surface: A trainee unexpectedly gets the answer correct and is thrilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges THEN as ENTH.
explanation.definitionFit: To captivate or charm someone is to give them great pleasure, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Young infant, exceptionally neat one

indicators.note: exceptionally hints at something out of the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A baby who is unusually tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: A newborn baby, under four weeks old, is the medical term used here.

clue.text: Move quickly as one destined to go on board?

definitions.text: one destined to go on board?
definitions.meaning: a missile thrown at a dartboard in the pub game

explanation.surface: Someone rushes to catch a ship or train they are booked onto.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to dash and the small pointed missile thrown at a board.

clue.text: Some mother almost seen as a goddess

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A mother who is nearly worshipped as divine.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth she was queen of the gods, wife of Zeus, a deity.

clue.text: Check feature of wine glass

definitions.meaning: to stop or stanch a flow
the slender part between bowl and foot

explanation.surface: Inspecting the shape of a glass of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to staunch a flow and also the thin shaft of a drinking glass.

clue.text: See 8
Personal account from Conservative on shelf I repeatedly moved

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after
moved means shifted about, so these letters are put in a new order
repeatedly says the letter I appears twice

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A politician's memoir propped on a bookshelf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' means I is used twice in the anagram fodder that 'moved' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A full biography of someone's life is a personal record or story.

clue.text: Outcry putting off our reticent person

indicators.note: putting off means removing, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: a clamour is a loud public outcry

explanation.surface: A public protest makes a quiet person wary.
explanation.walkthrough: CLAMOUR loses OUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who will not talk is said to clam up, so a shellfish stands for a taciturn type.

clue.text: Disorder of some French chaps taking time crossing mountains

indicators.note: crossing means spanning, so the outer pieces straddle the inner one
taking means the next piece is added on

parts.note: de is French for some, as in pas de pain
men are chaps
a range is a chain of mountains

explanation.surface: French men taking their time to trek over the Alps cause chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some French' is de, the French partitive used after a negative; 'crossing' wraps the outer pieces around the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Derangement is mental disturbance or general confusion, a synonym of chaos.
